concerns.text: T009 is tagged [P] but its body says it 'Sequentially invoke download → validate → clean → disproportionality → sensitivity → temporal stages' — it consumes the outputs/modules of T002–T008. A [P] tag here is unsafe: it implies T009 can run in parallel with the very tasks it orchestrates. Remove the [P] tag.

The stated execution order says 'T009 after T004', but T009's own description invokes the sensitivity and temporal stages (T007, T008). T009 must be ordered after T007 and T008 (or after T006–T008), not merely after T004; as written an implementer following the order line would run the orchestrator before its final stages exist.

T005 is tagged [P] and listed as independent of T004, but its verification requires 'a small DataFrame built from real cleaned rows (or a 2-row slice of data/processed/cleaned.parquet)' — an artifact produced only by T004. Either drop the [P] tag / order T005 after T004, or rewrite the test to use a self-contained fixture DataFrame so T005 is genuinely parallel-safe.
